title: How do we write the nearest neighbours of a number?
description: A number is rounded to the thousand, ten thousand, lakh, ten lakh and crore by keeping the digits up to a place and looking at the next digit. Two numbers get their five nearest neighbours each. Keeko then raises a hand, thinking the digits after the place are only dropped.
teaching_notes: One idea: to round, keep the digits up to the place, look at the next digit, and go up by one when it is five or more. Ask the class which digit decides the rounding before any place is chosen. Watch for students who drop the digits after the place instead of looking at the next digit.

source: Write the five nearest neighbours of (a) 3,87,69,957 and (b) 29,05,32,481
video_script.why: The child has met the nearest neighbours of one number in the book, and now writes them for two new numbers.
video_script.substitution: Keep the digits up to the place, look at the next digit, go up by one when it is five or more, and make the rest zeros.
video_script.anchor: The two numbers 3,87,69,957 and 29,05,32,481 with the five places thousand, ten thousand, lakh, ten lakh and crore listed beside them.
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko keeps the digit eight at the ten lakh place and drops the rest, so the nearest ten lakh comes out as three crore eighty lakh. The next digit is seven, which is five or more, so the eight goes up to nine.
video_script.payoff_line: Each number now has its five nearest neighbours

final_answer.spoken: for the first number, three crore eighty seven lakh seventy thousand twice, three crore eighty eight lakh, three crore ninety lakh and four crore; for the second number, twenty nine crore five lakh thirty two thousand, twenty nine crore five lakh thirty thousand, twenty nine crore five lakh, twenty nine crore ten lakh and twenty nine crore

never_show: the rounded numbers before the answer beat
maths_rules: ten thousand: keep 3,87,6, next digit 9, up, 3,87,70,000
lakh: keep 3,87, next digit 6, up, 3,88,00,000; ten lakh: keep 3,8, next digit 7, up, 3,90,00,000; crore: keep 3, next digit 8, up, 4,00,00,000
ten thousand: keep 29,05,3, next digit 2, stays, 29,05,30,000; lakh: keep 29,05, next digit 3, stays, 29,05,00,000
ten lakh: keep 29,0, next digit 5, up, 29,10,00,000; crore: keep 29, next digit 0, stays, 29,00,00,000
the slip: 3,87,69,957 to the ten lakh is 3,90,00,000, not 3,80,00,000, because the next digit 7 is five or more
video_script.design: One idea: keep up to the place, look at the next digit, five or more goes up. Wrong idea: Keeko drops the digits after the place. The anchor stays all video; the working band builds in the idea part; no hard clear.
